sections.title: Ask anything. Do something with the answer.
sections.lead: Applications, registrations, waivers, guest details and feedback, built from a template in minutes. People fill them in on their phone with no app. Every answer lands on the right person’s record, and an approved applicant can be offered a place at your event.

sections.title: Each one knows what happens next.

items.title: Applications
items.body: Ask who they are and why they want to come, then approve each one.
items.then: Then: offer approved people a place

items.title: Registrations
items.body: A place request with the questions your event needs.
items.then: Then: add them to the event’s guest list

items.title: Guest details
items.body: Dietary needs, pace, level, team name, accessibility.
items.then: Then: it’s on their record for the night

items.title: Waivers
items.body: Terms they read and sign before a run, a climb or a session.
items.then: Then: a signed receipt for that event

items.title: Feedback
items.body: Ratings and a private note after the event.
items.then: Then: it rolls into your event feedback

items.title: Surveys
items.body: What time, what format, what next. Ask your community.
items.then: Then: answers and charts, ready to export

A choice that jumps to a later section still opens it, and anything a {{brand.name}} form can’t do yet is listed for you to rebuild by hand.

items.question: Do people need an app to fill in a form?
items.answer: No. Forms open in the phone’s browser, from a link, a QR code or an embed on your site.

items.question: Can I use a form without a {{brand.name}} event?
items.answer: Yes. A survey or an application works on its own. You can offer people a place at an event later.

items.question: Can questions depend on earlier answers?
items.answer: Yes. Show a question only when an earlier answer calls for it.

items.question: Can people upload a file?
items.answer: Yes. Add an upload question, and the file is kept with their answers.

items.question: Can I collect a signature?
items.answer: Yes, with a waiver form: the terms, the acknowledgement and a signature, kept as a receipt for that event.

items.question: Can I bring in my Google Forms applications?
items.answer: Yes. Export the answers as a CSV or Excel file and import them, matching your columns to the questions. Import brings in answers; new forms are built in {{brand.name}}.

items.question: Where do form fees go?
items.answer: Into your own Razorpay account, by UPI or card.

items.question: Does filling in a form sign people up for marketing?
items.answer: No. Hearing from you later is a separate yes, which you can ask for on the form.

sections.title: About bringing a form over.

items.question: Can I bring my Google Form over?
items.answer: Yes. Paste the link to a public Google Form and {{brand.name}} makes a private draft form with its sections, questions and choices. Anything it can’t bring across, such as a grid question, is listed for you to rebuild.

items.question: Does it bring the answers people already gave?
items.answer: No. It brings the form, not its answers. To bring past answers in, export them as a CSV or Excel file and import them into the form.
